summary:
MOONLIT is an interactive scientific decision-support system developed to help evaluate potential lunar landing sites. Through a 3D lunar environment, it brings together three key capabilities: analysing Sun and Earth visibility at selected locations, visualising how these conditions change over time, and comparing multiple landing sites.

By incorporating geometric and terrain-based obstruction, MOONLIT helps users understand how lunar topography, location and timing influence illumination and direct Earth visibility. Its Mission Planner provides detailed scientific analysis, while Guide mode makes the application and its underlying concepts easier to understand.

MOONLIT addresses the challenge of making complex lunar landing-site analysis more accessible and intuitive. It aims to support informed exploration of potential landing locations while helping students, the public and mission planners better understand the scientific challenges of lunar exploration.
details:
MOONLIT combines three interconnected tools:

  • Site Search: Evaluates Sun illumination and direct Earth visibility at a selected lunar coordinate and time.
  • Timeline: Uses time-sampled scientific data, playback and charts to show how Sun and Earth positions and visibility change over a selected interval.
  • Comparison: Evaluates two or three lunar locations using shared or independent time intervals.

The system accounts for both geometric and terrain-based obstructions, providing scientific measurements, visibility summaries and time-based events. Its Guide mode provides instructions and concise explanations of the scientific terminology.

Benefits and objectives: The platform makes lunar site analysis easier to explore, interpret and compare. We hope to improve public understanding of lunar exploration while providing an accessible interface for investigating important landing-site conditions.

Technology used:

  • Frontend: React, TypeScript and Vite.
  • 3D graphics: Three.js and React Three Fiber.
  • Backend: Python and FastAPI.
  • Scientific tools and data: NASA SPICE and LOLA lunar topography data.
  • Development: Visual Studio Code, Git and GitHub.
  • Deployment: Cloudflare Pages and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure.

What makes it particularly distinctive is the integration of three perspectives: examining a specific location, experiencing how conditions evolve over time, and comparing multiple sites. We also go beyond the analysis itself by introducing Guide mode, which helps users understand the tools and the science behind their results.
